newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian consumer confidence stronger - poll.
newsitem.headline: Canadian consumer confidence stronger - poll.

text.p: Canadian consumers are significantly more confident about the economy than they were a year ago, an Angus Reid/Southam News poll said on Monday.

Fifty-five percent of those polled from January 21-27 said the national economy was in good shape, 18 points higher than a year earlier. Thirty-seven percent said the econony was poor and seven percent said very poor.

The overall assessment was unchanged from November and only marginally better than last autumn but markedly better than January 1996, when 37 percent said good/very good and 63 per cent said poor/very poor.
The mood in Alberta was best (76 percent positive), followed by British Columbia (63 percent), Manitoba/Saskatchewan (61 percent) and Ontario (58 percent).
But in Quebec and Atlantic Canada, 58 percent and 56 percent gave the national economy a "thumbs down."
For the year ahead, 39 percent expected the economy to improve, 18 percent to worsen and 42 percent saw no change.
